name: Religious Zionism
summary: Religious Zionism holds that Jewish national return to the Land of Israel and a Jewish state are part of a divine plan of redemption, and that Torah, people and land form one whole. Following Rav Kook, it values even secular Zionists as unwitting agents of that process and wants the state to let Jews live by halakha. Its dominant present form, shaped by Zvi Yehuda Kook and the settler movement, rejects territorial concessions and gives the land's sanctity priority over diplomacy.
scope: The mainstream Dati Leumi movement in the Kookian line: Abraham Isaac Kook, his son Zvi Yehuda Kook and Gush Emunim, plus today's Religious Zionist Party, with Rabbi Yehuda Amital's moderate view noted as a minority current. It excludes the Haredi anti-Zionist view and treats the Kahanist fringe as outside the mainstream. Economic and technology questions are mostly inferred, so those answers are low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Religious Zionism has no healthcare doctrine; the Torah-and-labor Hapoel Hamizrachi tradition and Israel's existing public system make support the default, but parties prioritise other issues.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Hapoel Hamizrachi labor wing favoured worker protection while today's right-leaning parties are split on economics, so there is no settled line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents range from religious-labor traditions to market-oriented Likud voters; economics is not defining for the movement.

public-ownership.rationale: Torah va'Avodah drew on socialist ideas historically, but today's mainstream and party voters mostly accept a market economy, so adherents lean against nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement has no tax doctrine and adherents are divided between religious-labor and right-liberal economics.

unions-good.rationale: Hapoel Hamizrachi was a religious labor federation, yet modern adherents' views on unions are mixed and not ideologically defined.

property-fundamental.rationale: No distinctive property doctrine; halakha respects property but the movement does not make it an overriding right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation is not addressed by the ideology and adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Torah ethics stress charity and care for the weak, and religious-education and large-family communities depend on state support, so adherents tend to reject welfare cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: The religious kibbutz movement practised collective ownership, but it is a small historic strand and not a goal of the present mainstream.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-first outlook after terrorism makes adherents broadly accepting of surveillance, inferred rather than documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Orthodox social conservatism and the movement's moral-education emphasis make adherents opposed to legalising recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split: concern about incitement against Jews coexists with distrust of speech limits that could be turned against right-wing and religious speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Religious Zionism looks to Torah and rabbinic authority rather than a bypassing strongman; adherents on the right back strong government but not circumventing institutions in principle.

state-harmful.rationale: Kook and his heirs regard the State of Israel as holy, the beginning of redemption, so the claim that the state is harmful is rejected emphatically.

limit-guns.rationale: Settler communities and the right-wing base favour civilian arms for self-defence, though gun policy is not a doctrinal matter.

empower-police-military.rationale: The movement prizes military service (Hesder) and security; parties campaign for stronger police and army powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Orthodox sexual ethics and Torah-based public values make legalising prostitution unacceptable to adherents.

decide-locally.rationale: Strong national-centred outlook; Zvi Yehuda Kook treated the land and nation as a unity, though settler communities value local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Adherents combine repentance (teshuva) values with tough-on-crime and anti-terror punitive stances; no unified view.

traditional-family.rationale: Orthodox Judaism centres on the traditional family, and the party opposes recognising same-sex marriage on religious grounds.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Religious Zionist Party opposes recognising same-sex marriage on religious grounds, and Orthodox halakha does not recognise it; only a small Meimad-style minority differs.

abortion-legal.rationale: Halakha permits abortion only in limited circumstances, mainly for the mother's health, so adherents oppose a general legal right.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious Zionism aims at a Jewish state in which Jews can live by Torah, and the party seeks more Torah study and religious education funding.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern of the ideology; adherents tend to see affirmative-action style policies as foreign to its priorities.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Orthodox teaching holds male and female as divinely ordained categories, and the movement resists gender-theory curricula.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The People of Israel is one of the three pillars of the movement, and Kook and Amital stress national Jewish renewal and heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Kook's redemption unfolds in stages and the movement values halakha and established institutions, though settlers also act ahead of the state.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Aliyah by Jews is encouraged, while the party favours expelling asylum-seekers; on immigration in general adherents are split because statement is not specific to Jews.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents distrust the UN as hostile to Israel and reject outside bodies constraining Israeli sovereignty over the land.

free-trade.rationale: The movement has no trade doctrine and adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: The party and adherents put Jewish national interests and security first; national particularity is central to Kook's thought.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust the human-rights framing used against Israel yet value moral limits on force, so views are split.

open-borders.rationale: A Jewish state with defended borders is the movement's goal, and the party backs expelling asylum-seekers.

limit-growth.rationale: No environmental doctrine; adherents favour settlement and building, and Kook's cultivation of the land as a mitzvah leans toward development.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not part of the ideology; adherents on the right are generally sceptical of drastic state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Israeli religious Zionists embrace technology yet the ideology holds redemption comes through Torah, so there is no settled view.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents revere the state, though Zvi Yehuda Kook came to see the government as illegitimate and some settler activists defy it; broadly the mainstream rejects revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement defers to rabbinic Torah authority, but the party attacks the unelected judiciary and elites, so general expert rule is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: Religious Zionism never favoured a planned economy; even its labor wing was cooperative rather than centrally planned.

socialized-markets.rationale: The religious kibbutz tradition is sympathetic, but the modern mainstream is mostly indifferent.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents have no position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No doctrine; halakha treats inheritance as a firm family right and the right-leaning base opposes heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the base favours work and supports welfare for the needy without unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: No trade doctrine in the movement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not a topic for the ideology; adherents are split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cooperative settlement ideas exist in Hapoel Hamizrachi but there is no defined position today.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Entirely foreign to the ideology, which accepts an ordinary monetary economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; adherents accept conventional state institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Torah va'Avodah labor tradition had a corporate flavour but modern adherents have no position.

one-party-rule.rationale: Religious Zionism competes in a multi-party democratic system and sees Torah, not a party, as the guide.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Messianic hopes include a Davidic kingship eventually, but a modern hereditary monarch is not a programme; adherents are split or indifferent.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents take part in Israeli democracy, yet Zvi Yehuda Kook held Torah law over referendums, and the party seeks to curb the judiciary, so democracy is not held supreme.

direct-votes.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook held that referendums could not overturn Torah law, and the movement does not push direct democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: The unity of the land and the Jewish state is sacrosanct; the movement rejects dividing it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kook believed in a distinct role for the Jewish people and Torah scholars but no doctrine of born rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject political violence against Jews, but Zvi Yehuda Kook justified force against Arabs who rejected Jewish rights and the Kahanist strand supports it.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement values military service, but it does not teach war as character building; adherents are split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement wants a Jewish state in which Jews live by Torah and halakha, and the Kooks reject strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook ranked Torah law above secular law; mainstream adherents want halakha to shape state law though they disagree on how far.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement is statist about defence and sees the state as sacred.

military-superiority.rationale: Military strength is seen as essential to Jewish survival in Israel, with Hesder yeshivot producing combat soldiers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The goal is a Jewish state with a Jewish majority, and Kook saw a unique Jewish national soul; this is national-religious rather than racial.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kook's thought rests on divine providence and holds that Torah rather than Marxism guides a just society.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not part of the ideology; Torah ethics emphasise charity rather than equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Adherents view Jews as the indigenous people of the Land of Israel, so the principle is read in their favour, but the statement is not framed by the ideology.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents reject the colonialism frame applied to Zionism and see no such duty.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement is Jewish-national rather than pan-religious; adherents are split or indifferent.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Torah values stress duty, charity and the national good rather than self-interest as a moral ideal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Torah as a system of obligations and Amital's call to be a holy nation place communal duty first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Kook held that animals and nature had value and viewed meat as a temporary concession, though this is one thinker's view.

limit-population.rationale: Orthodox Judaism encourages large families, and adherents oppose population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not a view of the movement; adherents embrace the modern state and its technology.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Religious Zionism has no doctrine on the pace of technological change, and its emphasis on halakha and established institutions gives adherents no reason to favour disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: No doctrine; halakhic caution against tampering with the body coexists with Israeli technophilia.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The ideology puts authority in Torah and human leaders; inferred rejection.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No doctrine, and security-first outlook conflicts with libertarian privacy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kook looked to a Torah-based future redemption rather than a lost order, though it draws on the ancient Jewish commonwealth; adherents are divided.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Religious Zionism is guided by Torah principles and not judged by pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: Settlers used direct action to found settlements through Gush Emunim, while mainstream adherents work through the Knesset.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a topic for the ideology.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign; Kook saw cultivating the land as a mitzvah. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not a doctrine, though Torah ethics stress charity.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Kook's thought rejects a Marxist analysis of society.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Kook explicitly saw a just society guided by Torah rather than Marxism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: The religious kibbutzim practised it, but it is not the movement's goal today.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory is rejected; the movement sees war as arising from hostility to Jewish rights.

taxation-theft.rationale: Orthodox Judaism accepts the authority of the state and the community to tax.

harm-principle.rationale: Halakha and Torah public values go beyond harm prevention, and Amital calls for a holy nation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective national rights, and Kook's view of the Jewish people as an organic unit, contradict an individual-only conception.

conscription.rationale: Military service is seen as vital to Jewish survival and the movement supports universal service and Hesder.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Aliyah and staying in the land are valued; the statement runs against attachment to the state.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is regarded as holy by Kook's school, not a business.

media-academia-power.rationale: The party attacks left-leaning media, universities and courts, though this is a political stance rather than doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Kook claimed a qualitative difference between Jewish and non-Jewish souls but on spiritual grounds, not genetics, and the ideology does not teach racial ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: The movement uses party politics, with no program for corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Religious Zionism seeks Torah society but not a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kook framed Zionism as national rebirth and redemption, though the statement's decadence frame is not his.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook ruled out aggressive war while some party members seek annexation of the West Bank, and the statement is broader than the land claim.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Orthodox thought holds Torah truth to be objective.

universal-morality.rationale: Torah morality is regarded as universal in claim, and Amital stresses moral treatment of non-Jews, though Kook's particularism complicates this.

single-common-good.rationale: Torah-guided society implies one good, but Israel's party politics are pluralistic.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The right of the Jewish people to the Land of Israel is the movement's central pillar, based on divine promise and Zionism as redemption.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Aliyah and ingathering of exiles are core religious-Zionist commitments, and the Law of Return reflects them.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hebrew revival was part of national rebirth, and religious Zionists treat Hebrew as the Torah's language and the state's.

school-vouchers.rationale: The party seeks more funding for religious education and its community runs a separate state-religious school stream.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed by Kook's thought or party platforms, and adherents divide along ordinary right-left economic lines.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kook emphasised moral renewal through Torah but not rule by example instead of laws.

national-self-determination.rationale: Jewish self-determination in the Land of Israel is the point of the movement, though adherents tend to apply it with priority to the Jewish people.

force-without-un.rationale: Adherents distrust the UN and insist Israel act on its own security judgement.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Faith and Torah are central; the claim that reason should be the only guide contradicts the ideology.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Torah concern for the stranger conflicts with the party's anti-asylum stance.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split, partly because of the haredi dispute.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kook's synthesis ideal and Torah va'Avodah favoured unity among Jews rather than class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage and tradition are central to the ideology. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

dominated-front.rationale: Not part of the movement; adherents orient to the West and Judaism.

workers-nation.rationale: The labor wing was nationalist, but the proposition is not distinctive here.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Orthodox tradition has distinct roles, though religious Zionist women serve in national service, study and public life.

ban-interest.rationale: Halakha forbids interest between Jews but the movement does not seek a state ban on lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of religious Zionism; Amital urges respectful treatment of non-Jews, and the mainstream rejects it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not part of the ideology; the movement's sources discuss land, Torah and the state, so adherents have no collective view.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Jewish immigrants are expected to join the national culture, but the statement is general and adherents split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a doctrine of the movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Israel's party-list proportional system is the framework within which religious Zionist parties operate; no doctrinal view.

national-mission.rationale: Kook saw Israel as a light unto the nations bringing salvation to the world, though through Torah not by imposing government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Adherents generally reject the structural patriarchy diagnosis, though Orthodox feminism exists.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party attacks judicial and media elites, but corruption of politicians generally is not a doctrinal claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Halakha values life and the family, and the idea is foreign to the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Adherents strongly back the IDF and resist external legal accountability, though not necessarily internal.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement expects the state to pursue Torah-based public values.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Orthodox Judaism discourages marriage outside the faith, but on religious not racial grounds.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kook asserted a qualitative difference between Jewish and non-Jewish souls, while Amital and mainstream stress respect for non-Jews; the strands split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not relevant; the ideology rejects Marxist socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents regard Zionism as the return of an indigenous people to its homeland and reject the colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The movement wants halakha to influence personal status law and the state rabbinate keeps religious jurisdiction over marriage.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox control of Jewish conversion is defended, though the statement's general form is not discussed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Kook idealised vegetarianism but did not propose banning slaughter, and Jewish law permits it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The community built state-religious schools (Mamlachti Dati), with over 60 high schools, and the party wants more religious education.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents participate in democracy but Zvi Yehuda Kook ranked Torah above referendums, so legitimacy is not seen as resting only on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance is not a concern of the movement's thinkers or parties, so no position can be drawn from its principles.

population-transfer.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook allowed Arabs to stay if they accepted Jewish sovereignty, while the Kahanist fringe and some party figures advocate transfer; mainstream adherents are split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Adherents accept the legitimacy of state force and war, including pre-emptive defence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kook saw progress as a divine synthesis of opposing forces rather than competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents support banning anti-Israel parties, although Kach itself was banned, so views vary.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican idea of freedom is never discussed in the movement's sources, and its Torah-centred outlook gives no lean either way.

separated-powers.rationale: Adherents support checks in principle but the party seeks political control of the judiciary.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Torah ethics emphasise charity and justice for the poor, but this is not a program of the movement.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the ideology, and the sources show no stance on it from Religious Zionist thinkers or parties.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law on strikes is not addressed in the movement's sources; its historical labor wing and its right-leaning voters would pull in opposite directions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Large families are valued and the claim is not accepted.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Adherents value a cohesive Jewish national majority, but the movement does not state this as a general sociology.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Security-minded adherents accept emergency powers, while the Zionist right also emphasises law; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed by the ideology, and adherents hold mixed economic views, so the answer is a neutral placeholder.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents compete as an opposition at times and do not favour party media control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Foreign; the IDF is a state army that adherents revere. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Jews have the Law of Return while non-Jewish naturalisation is not addressed; split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators is not a Religious Zionist issue in the sources I read, and nothing in its principles bears on it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Rabbinic authority guides adherents more than party discipline; no clear doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adherents defend Jewish national sovereignty and distrust supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Israel's parliamentary system and the symbolic presidency are accepted.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Judaism has no church; the Chief Rabbinate model is a rabbinic authority, so the statement fits poorly.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rabbinic guidance is central and Zvi Yehuda Kook put Torah first, yet the movement supports elected government and the Hardal strand differs.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Foreign to a movement that prizes military service. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents value modesty and public values, but no doctrine of state censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the movement's thought, which concerns the land and Torah rather than executive tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections do not figure in the movement's sources, and its reverence for rabbinic authority offers no guidance on them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents support the US alliance and security cooperation.

people-in-arms.rationale: The movement favours a strong professional army, though it supports civilian settler defence.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kook valued working the land, and settlement is a religious ideal, yet no claim that rural life is morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook condemned the 1947 partition and wanted the whole land of Israel; the statement is general.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The party attacks elites but the movement values Torah and academic education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kook held that Jews have a unique role, and traditionalists reject cultural equivalence.

death-penalty.rationale: The Religious Zionist Party and its allies campaign for the death penalty for terrorists.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox adherents oppose gender-equality and sex education framed outside religious values.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Kook was open to evolution as part of divine process, and the state-religious school stream teaches science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Orthodox modesty norms and Torah public values favour legal restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Law of Return reflects descent-based Jewish belonging, which religious Zionists strongly endorse for Jews.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want Hebrew's primacy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents seek protection for religious practice, but exemptions for minorities are not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The movement values custom and Torah observance over eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries lies outside the ideology; its sources show no view on global finance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The claim concerns anti-colonial independence movements, which Religious Zionism never framed in economic terms, so no position follows.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook ranked Torah above referendums; the movement has no constitution rewrite programme.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Torah values emphasise charity but the movement is not internationalist.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Self-reliance in defence is strongly valued, and Israel's own deterrent is accepted.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How Israel's president is chosen is not a question the movement's thinkers addressed; adherents accept the present parliamentary choice.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not covered by the movement's sources, so adherents have no collective view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook ruled out yielding any part of the land, comparing it to eating pork, and the party opposes territorial concessions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Torah teachings combine property rights with duties, but there is no defined position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not a topic of the ideology.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation under uncertainty is not addressed by Kook or the parties, and adherents split by general right-left outlook.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents value allies, but the statement is general.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents deny that Judea and Samaria are occupied, regarding them as the Jewish homeland, and some seek to annex the West Bank.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement wants more religious institutional power, not less; the Chief Rabbinate is an established institution.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Israel's presidency is a symbolic nonpartisan office that adherents accept.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unity of the land is sacred, so adherents accept force to prevent separation, though not directly addressed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A region keeping its own system conflicts with the national unity the movement seeks, though settlers' local autonomy is valued.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Judaism rejects divinised rulers, though Kook sanctified the state and not the head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not part of Religious Zionist doctrine, and the sources I read give no stance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Torah education stresses upbringing while holding free will.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Torah law binds even the king in Jewish thought, and the movement places Torah above rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is unrelated to the movement's concerns with land, Torah and nation, so it takes no stand.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical idea of mixing rule by few and many is not discussed by the movement's thinkers, so nothing indicates a lean.

leader-cult.rationale: Judaism rejects idolising leaders, although rabbis hold wide respect.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside the ideology's sources, and Orthodox family traditions give no clear presumption either way.

land-redistribution.rationale: No doctrine; adherents lean against forcible takings, though cultivating the land is valued.

refugee-return.rationale: Adherents reject return of Palestinian refugees and descendants, since it would undermine Jewish sovereignty.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The claim to the land rests on divine promise and Jewish settlement, not on co-ethnics living there; adherents are somewhat open to the principle.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Halakha treats apostasy as grave but modern religious Zionists accept a democratic state that does not punish it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Adherents value modest dress but do not seek to require full covering by law.

common-currency.rationale: Adherents favour national sovereignty over supranational arrangements.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook's strand gives Arabs no collective autonomy in a Jewish state; inferred from the sources' account of attitudes to Arabs.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Return to the Land of Israel and a Jewish state are central pillars, so persecuted Jews are expected to build the homeland, not stay in exile.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rav Kook sees redemption as a divine plan working through history, an idealist rather than materialist view.

ban-cartels.rationale: No doctrine on competition law; the Hapoel Hamizrachi tradition and right-leaning parties differ.

no-bailouts.rationale: No settled line on rescues; adherents are not documented as taking a side.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Religious Zionist Party supports curbing the judiciary, which is described in its programme, and Z. Y. Kook placed Torah above secular law.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox gender norms in the movement; quotas are not documented.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the movement's market-leaning right-wing politics; not addressed in the sources.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents are split between labour and market traditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: The labour wing stressed duty and settlement as ideals, while current parties are market-leaning, so adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rav Kook sees redemption unfolding by divine plan, and the mainstream works through legal settlement; fringe underground groups differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary priestly status exists in halakha but political titles are not an issue for the movement.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on Jewish peoplehood and Torah; Religious Zionist education centres Jewish and Israeli history, though no doctrine on curricula was found.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's religious and nationalist stance; it has no stated view on defending planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the movement works within Israel's direct parliamentary elections and has no stated case for delegate-chosen office.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement wants the state to let Jews live by halakha and values the Chief Rabbinate's religious role, which is an official status for Orthodox Judaism; the question is applied by analogy.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement rejects territorial concessions and Palestinian territorial claims, placing the land's sanctity above them.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Its dominant form rejects territorial concessions and holds that the land's sanctity overrides the wishes of the inhabitants, so a vote on sovereignty is opposed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement does not address postcolonial borders; inferred as neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents range from settlers living modestly to urban modern Orthodox, so inferred as neutral.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the movement leads Jewish settlement in the West Bank and opposes limits on settling in the land.

equal-conscription.rationale: Adherents are split: Religious Zionists serve in the army but many rabbis oppose women's conscription; no shared position.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Religious Zionism treats the Land of Israel as sacred and Zvi Yehuda Kook gave its sanctity priority over diplomacy, so the bond and duty to hold it are central.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Halakha demands due process, so killing without trial is inferred to be rejected; not addressed in the sources.

close-ties-china.rationale: Religious Zionism is closely aligned with the West and Israel's ties to the United States; inferred, not addressed in the sources.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Concern for Jews abroad follows from the people-land-Torah unity, though the statement concerns neighbouring states; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: No documented position; Torah views of land ownership cut both ways, so inferred as neutral.

self-ownership.rationale: Halakha binds the individual to commandments while protecting person and labour; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No economic doctrine in the sources; inferred as neutral.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No economic doctrine in the sources; inferred as neutral.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement works through rabbinic institutions, parties and yeshivot rather than bypassing groups; inferred from its organisation.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Economic questions are mostly inferred; adherents are split, so neutral.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The movement runs its own religious party and wants the state to let Jews live by halakha, so religious organisation of politics is accepted.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Kook's thought embraces secular Zionist progress as part of redemption, so combining modernity with tradition is inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Halakha requires the husband's consent to a get, and the movement wants the state to follow halakha and ranks Torah above secular law.

national-resource-control.rationale: Sovereign Jewish control of the land's resources follows from the state's purpose; inferred, not addressed in the sources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: No distributive doctrine; adherents are split between market and Torah-and-labor traditions, so inferred as neutral.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The movement does not address racial advancement as such; inferred as neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Zvi Yehuda Kook ranked Torah law above secular law, so adherents tend to hold that law lacking divine justice has no authority; inferred from that.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The Torah-and-labor tradition values work, so a lean against ending work is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Jewish national sovereignty and resistance to outside dictation of territory suggest preference for independent powers; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: No economic doctrine of value; the religious framing of labour suggests value is not purely labour-created, inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Religious Zionism joins love of land and nation with the Jewish people but has no doctrine on workers' solidarity abroad; adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Religious identity and the sanctity of the land come before economic class politics; inferred from the movement's priorities.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A communist party is atheist and incompatible with Torah-based statehood; inferred from the movement's principles.

missingStatements.text: Settling in the land of one's ancestral homeland is a religious duty.
missingStatements.rationale: Settlement and cultivation of the land are described as a mitzvah, and Religious Zionists led the settlement drive.
missingStatements.declined: Religious framing of positions already covered by jewish-state-israel, no-land-for-peace and diaspora-return-right.

missingStatements.text: Laws of marriage and divorce should follow religious law rather than civil law.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement wants a Jewish state in which Jews live by halakha, and Zvi Yehuda Kook ranked Torah law above secular law.

notes: Strands differ: Amital's moderate current views the state as an imperfect beginning of redemption and urges respect for non-Jews, while the Hardal and Kahanist strands are more statist-halakhic and more hostile to Arabs. Mainstream answers here lean to the Kookian settler mainstream. Economic answers are weakly founded.
